podcast.title: Acute Anxiety Diagnosis
podcast.body: Meg White suffered from acute anxiety, which was officially cited as the reason for The White Stripes' unexpected cancellation of their planned tour dates in the United States and the UK in 2007. This condition had a significant impact on the band's ability to tour and ultimately contributed to their separation. "Meg White sufició a la ansiedad aguda."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: Por qué White Stripes desaparecieron en su mejor momento?

podcast.title: Brother and Sister Myth
podcast.body: A persistent myth claimed that Jack and Meg White were brother and sister, which is entirely false. Jack Gillis (his birth name) was the tenth of ten children from a Catholic family in Detroit, with no sister named Meg, while Meg White was from Gross Point Farms with one sister, Heather, and no brothers. This false narrative was deliberately cultivated by Jack White in early interviews, where he referred to Meg as his "little sister," even after their marriage certificate was posted online in 2001. "When you see a band that's two pieces, husband and wife, boyfriend and girlfriend, you think, oh, I see. When their brother and sister, you go, oh, that's interesting. You care more about the music, not the relationship, whether they're trying to save their relationship by being in a band together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Drummer for The White Stripes
podcast.body: Meg White is the drummer for The White Stripes, known for her minimalist yet impactful style that defined the duo's sound. "and of course Meg White of the White Stripes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reluctance to Fame
podcast.body: Meg White possessed a timid personality and was generally reluctant towards media attention, which became increasingly challenging as The White Stripes achieved massive fame. She did not enjoy touring or interviews, and with the band's growing popularity, she began to withdraw more significantly from the public eye. "Meg White tiene una persona timida y reacia la atención mediática."

xref.title: Marriage and Name Change (September 21, 1996)
xref.body: Jack Gillis married Meg White on September 21, 1996. In a departure from tradition, Jack adopted Meg's last name, becoming Jack White. "They started dating seriously. That continued until they got married on September 21, 1996. And in a change in tradition, Jack took her last name. So Jack Gillis became Jack White."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation and Early Releases (1997-1998)
xref.body: Jack and Meg White began performing in 1997 and started releasing singles in 1998, utilizing various independent labels that were willing to sign them. "Jack and Meg White first started hacking about in 1997 and releasing singles in 1998. They used a variety of indie labels. Whoever would have them, basically."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Meg White's Introduction to Drums (July 14, 1997)
xref.body: Meg White, who had no prior drumming experience, unexpectedly sat down at Jack's drum kit at home on July 14, 1997, and began playing. Jack described this impromptu drumming as "liberating and refreshing," leading him to suggest forming a band with her. "Jack had his drum kit set up at home and Meg suddenly decided to sit down and started bashing away. She had no idea what she was doing because she had no experience on the drums whatsoever. But I quote Jack, When she started to play the drums with me just on a lark, it felt liberating and refreshing. There was something in it that opened me up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Divorce (March 24, 2000)
xref.body: The marriage between Jack and Meg White ended in divorce on March 24, 2000. "But the marriage didn't last and they divorced on March 24, 2000."

xref.title: Meg White's Marriage (2009)
xref.body: Meg White married Jackson Smith, the son of punk legend Patti Smith, in 2009. The wedding ceremony took place in Jack White's backyard in Nashville. "And then when Meg married a guy named Jackson Smith, the son of punk legend, Patty Smith in 2009, the ceremony took place in Jack's backyard in Nashville."

xref.title: Breakup in 2011
xref.body: The White Stripes officially announced their breakup on February 2, 2011, stating it was for "a myriad of reasons, mostly to preserve what is beautiful and special about the band." The band had an influential run from 1997 through 2011, becoming a major part of the Indy Rock revival of the early 2000s alongside bands like The Strokes and Arctic Monkeys. The reasons for the split included Meg White's introverted nature and desire for a personal life, the end of her marriage to Jack White, and Jack's diverging musical ambitions. Following the breakup, Meg White receded into obscurity, while Jack White continued as a solo performer and music industry figure. "The official breakup announcement came on February 2, 2011."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Detroit Origins and Backgrounds
xref.body: Jack Gillis, a Detroit-area upholsterer and indie musician who nearly became a priest, met bartender Meg White. They became romantically involved and began jamming on Jack's music, with him teaching her to play drums. Their first gig was at The Gold Dollar in Detroit. "Jack Gillis, a Detroit area upholsterer and indie musician who almost decided to become a priest, met up with a bartender named Meg White."

xref.title: Formation and Persona
xref.body: Jack White, a former altar boy and furniture upholsterer, and Meg White, a shy, non-musical bartender, met, fell in love, married, and began jamming together. They cultivated a public persona of being brother and sister while releasing stripped-down bluesy garage rock music on indie labels. "A former altar boy and furniture a poster and the youngest child and a Detroit family of ten meets a shy, non-musical bartender. They fall in love, they get married, they start jamming together, pretend that their brother and sister and start releasing stripped down bluesy garage rock music on a series of indie labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Marriage and Divorce
xref.body: Jack and Meg White were married on September 21, 1996, with Jack Gillis adopting Meg's last name to become Jack White. They divorced in March 2000 but continued to be bandmates and friends, even attending and serving in each other's subsequent wedding parties. "The truth is that Jack and Meg were married on September 21, 1996, but then divorced in March of 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Lives
xref.body: After the band's dissolution, Meg White reportedly lives quietly in Detroit, while Jack White divides his time between Nashville and Detroit. They maintain infrequent contact. "As far as anyone could tell, Meg lives quietly in Detroit, and Jack spends most of his time in Nashville, although he goes back and forth to Detroit. They'll talk, but not that often."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Divorce Professional Amicability
xref.body: Despite their divorce, Jack and Meg White maintained a remarkably amicable professional relationship, continuing to work together as The White Stripes even as they became involved with other partners. "However, in an absolutely remarkable bit of amicability, they continued to work together as the white stripes, even as both of them got involved with other people."

xref.title: Priesthood Calling Abandoned for Guitar Amplifier – Jack White's Near-Seminary Life
xref.body: Jack White (born John Anthony Gillis) is the youngest of ten children of Gorman and Theresa Gillis, a devout Catholic couple in Detroit. Both parents worked for the Catholic Archdiocese of Detroit — his mother as a secretary, his father in maintenance. Jack served as an altar boy at the Church of the Holy Redeemer and, following in the footsteps of his six brothers, developed a sense of religious calling. He applied to and was accepted at a seminary in Wisconsin, but had a last-second change of heart when he realized he would not be permitted to bring his new guitar amplifier. He enrolled in public school instead. Had he gone, there would have been no White Stripes, no marriage and divorce to Meg White, and no subsequent marriage to model Karen Elson. "So talk about a decision that changes your life, huh?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

"Some ill-advised remarks to a group of vegans in a Brooklyn park in 2010, shots against Lady Gaga against Twitter against Clint Eastwood and even ex-wife Meg White in 2012."

xref.title: Relationship Obfuscation (Brother and Sister Pretense)
xref.body: Jack and Meg White deliberately obscured their true relationship, often pretending to be brother and sister to the public. This charade was maintained to "throw everybody off" and they notably refused to be interviewed separately. "At first, they pretended to be brother and sister just to throw everybody off. They refused to be interviewed separately."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Relationship of Jack and Meg White
xref.body: Contrary to a widely circulated myth, Jack (John Anthony Gillis) and Meg White are not brother and sister; they are ex-husband and wife. They met in Detroit in 1994, where Meghan Martha White was a bartender at Memphis Smoke, and John Anthony Gillis was an ex-furniture upholsterer. They married on September 12, 1996, with Jack taking Meg's last name in a reversal of tradition. They started their band, released albums, and then divorced on March 24, 2000, but remained friends and bandmates. The "brother and sister" claim began as a joke when the band started, and despite the truth being revealed when they gained fame, some people still refused to believe it. "For once and for all, they are not brother and sister. They are actually ex-husband and wife. John Anthony Gillis met Meghan Martha White in Detroit in 1994. She was a bartender at a place called Memphis Smoke, and he was an ex-furniture upholsterer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
